items.period: Shang period, broadly c. 1300–1046 BCE in the Commons project classification
items.tradition: Shang oracle script style; modern vector redraw based on a referenced J19580 image, not an ancient artifact photograph
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 北 in Shang oracle script style. The associated paleographic study cites oracle-bone examples for 北 and describes the two turned-away figures as the proposed graphic conception.
items.alt: Modern drawn oracle-script form of 北, shown as an early style candidate for comparison with later forms.
items.selection_reason: Provides an early graphic stage corresponding to inscription examples cited in the scholarly account and visually motivates the back-to-back interpretation. The linked paleographic context supports candidate identity; pixels remain for downstream inspection.
items.rights: Commons file page cites the Richard Sears website agreement and identifies the ancient-script SVG representation as public domain. Confirm the agreement's terms for this specific sourced redraw before reuse.

items.period: Shuowen Jiezi seal-form tradition, compiled in the Eastern Han (c. 100 CE); the file is a modern redraw of the dictionary style
items.tradition: Shuowen seal script style, not an excavated seal artifact
items.caption: A modern redraw of the 北 form presented in Shuowen seal-script style. Xu Shen's entry analyzes the character as two people back-to-back; this later dictionary form can be compared with the Shang-style candidate.
items.alt: Modern vector rendering of 北 in a Shuowen seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Pairs a documented later dictionary-style rendering with the early oracle-style candidate to illustrate continuity claimed by the paleographic study without implying that the image is an artifact.
items.rights: Commons licensing states the SVG representation is public domain; the file description also references the Richard Sears agreement.

limitations.text: Both proposed images are modern digital redrawings of historical script styles, not photographs or scans of ancient inscriptions. No pixel inspection occurred at the research stage.
The bronze-style file was not included because the Commons description page could not be opened to verify identity and reuse terms.
